Subject: Renewal: questions on upgrading dedicated pool from 8 → 16 GPUs

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the call yesterday. As we look to move forward with the renewal, a few items came up on our side before we sign the amendment:

- Start date and how billing will be prorated if we flip mid-cycle.
- Canary/rollout plan for activating the extra GPUs (we need minimal disruption to traffic).
- Concrete throughput guarantees and latency SLOs for the 16-GPU pool (we rely on a 95th pctl latency target for inference).
- What monitoring + alerting will be available to our ops team during cutover.

Can you send a proposed activation cadence and a draft amendment with the billing language? Procurement also wants any SLA credit language spelled out.

—Erin

LumenData

Erin — thanks for the clear list. High level response and a proposed plan below; I attached an internal ops checklist and a first-pass amendment for your review.

Plan summary (proposed):
1) Activation window: a 2-week phased canary starting on the agreed activation date. Week 1: enable 2x capacity to 20% of traffic, verify KV/cache heat and latency. Week 2: ramp to 50–100% as agreed with your SREs.
2) Billing/proration: Monthly commit for the renewal will reflect the new 16-GPU tier on the activation date. If we go live mid-billing-cycle, you will be billed pro-rata for the additional commit from activation day to month-end; next full month billed at the new commit.
3) Throughput & SLOs: We propose a baseline throughput guarantee equivalent to X tokens/sec per GPU (see amendment table) and a 95th percentile latency target of 120ms for the configured model family. SLA credit: 5% credit for monthly uptime < 99.5%, escalated tiers in the amendment.
4) Monitoring & alerts: we will provide a shared Dashboard link (read-only) for throughput, latency p95/p99, GPU utilization, and error rate. We'll create a shared PagerDuty route for the cutover window.

Next steps: I can update the amendment with any edits from procurement and send a DocuSign envelope once pricing language is confirmed. Attached: redwood-amendment-draft-v1.pdf (ops checklist inline).

If that looks good, are you available Wed morning for a 30-min cutover sync with your SREs?

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive — Dedicated Sales
Redwood Inference

Chloe — see numbers below and attached amendment v2. Key points:

Pricing & billing workback:
- Monthly reserved capacity price for 16-GPU pool: $74,000/month (this includes a 12% committed-discount vs spot/hosted list).
- If activation occurs mid-cycle: additional prorated charge = (days remaining in month / total days in month) * (difference between new and previous monthly commit). We will include an example line in the invoice (see billing-workback.csv).

SLA credits proposal:
- 99.5%–99.0% monthly uptime: 5% credit of monthly invoice.
- 99.0%–98.0%: 15% credit.
- <98.0%: 30% credit + priority remediation.

Canary thresholds (ops):
- Phase 1: 20% traffic for 72 hours. If p95 latency increases > 25% vs baseline for 15 consecutive minutes => rollback.
- Phase 2: 50% for 48 hours; same rollback condition.

I've attached the updated amendment (redwood-dedicated-amendment-draft-v2.pdf). Pricing is conservative; we can do a one-time activation credit if procurement needs to smooth the first-month cost.

—Marissa
VP, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
